string.text: Rendering mode. Static lighting (R1 and R4 static) uses baked light without dynamic shadows and suits weak PCs. The dynamic DX11 renderer (R4) adds shadows from every light, SSAO, volumetric light and other modern effects.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

A ready-made set of graphics settings, from Minimum to Ultra. Picking a preset overwrites the advanced settings. A good starting point: pick a preset, then tweak individual options.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], VRAM %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]

Screen resolution. Higher resolution gives a sharper image, but GPU load grows almost linearly with pixel count: 4K is about four times heavier than 1080p.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]
Overall image brightness. Adjust it to your monitor and room lighting.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]
Image contrast: the difference between dark and bright areas.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]

Gamma correction. Changes the brightness of mid-tones without touching black and white. Helps to see details in shadows.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]

Fullscreen mode. Usually gives slightly lower input latency and steadier frame rate than windowed mode. A window is handier for switching to other programs.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]
The game keeps running and rendering when its window is minimized or inactive. When off, the game pauses and does not load the PC while you are in another window. Does not affect in-game FPS.

Vertical sync: the frame rate is locked to the monitor refresh rate, removing screen tearing. Adds a little input latency. Caps FPS, so it reduces GPU load.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]reduces%c[default]

Screenshot file format. JPG is small but lossy. PNG and TGA are lossless but produce much larger files.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]

Density of grass and small vegetation. High density makes fields look lusher, but greatly increases the number of drawn objects.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], RAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Distance at which grass is visible. A larger distance hides the grass pop-in border but multiplies the amount of grass in frame.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

World draw distance. Objects beyond it are not drawn and are hidden by fog.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Level of detail of models at a distance. Higher values keep objects at full detail longer before switching to simplified versions.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Texture resolution. High quality gives crisp surfaces up close but needs a lot of video memory. When VRAM runs out you get stutter and texture streaming.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] VRAM %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], RAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Anisotropic filtering: keeps textures sharp at grazing angles (roads, floors, distant ground). Almost free on modern GPUs, 16x is recommended.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Extra detail textures layered over the base ones when surfaces are viewed up close.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Detail bump: fine surface relief up close using additional normal maps.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default], VRAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Parallax occlusion: stones, bricks and tiles look three-dimensional without extra geometry. Noticeably loads the GPU when many such surfaces are on screen.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

DX11 tessellation: the GPU subdivides surfaces into extra polygons so that relief becomes real geometry. One of the heaviest options.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]

Image scaling method. Linear simply stretches the image. DLSS (NVIDIA RTX GPUs) and FSR (any GPU) render at a lower resolution and reconstruct details, noticeably raising FPS. They also anti-alias the image.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]reduces%c[default], VRAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Internal resolution for DLSS and FSR. Native renders at full resolution (best anti-aliasing). Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance render fewer and fewer pixels: higher FPS, less detail.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]reduces%c[default]

DLSS neural network model.
%c[255,240,240,240]Auto%c[default] - the model is chosen by the quality mode.
%c[255,240,240,240]Convolutional neural network%c[default] - classic model, fastest but less stable.
%c[255,240,240,240]Transformer model%c[default] - more stable image and better anti-aliasing.
%c[255,240,240,240]2nd gen transformer model%c[default] (DLSS 4.5) - best quality, designed for RTX 40 and newer. RTX 20 and 30 owners should pick the convolutional network.
%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Internal resolution scale. Below 100% the frame is rendered smaller and upscaled (higher FPS, softer image). Above 100% is supersampling: a very sharp image at a huge cost.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

AMD CAS sharpening. Restores sharpness lost to anti-aliasing and upscaling. Too high a value causes halos on contrasting edges.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Smooths alpha-tested edges of foliage, grass and fences. Instead of a hard cutoff it uses noise that TAA, DLSS or FSR then resolve. Removes vegetation shimmering. Very expensive in forests and tall grass: more pixels of every leaf and grass blade pass, so overdraw grows.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]

Edge anti-aliasing method.
%c[255,240,240,240]FXAA%c[default] - fastest, slightly blurs the image.
%c[255,240,240,240]SMAA%c[default] - cleaner than FXAA with almost no blur.
%c[255,240,240,240]TAA%c[default] - best quality and no shimmering, but may ghost in motion.
%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], VRAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Shadow resolution of lamps, flashlights and other local lights. Higher values give sharp shadows without jagged edges.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Distance at which local lights keep shining and casting shadows. Affects how many lights are processed at once.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

NPC flashlights cast real light and shadows. At night in crowded places it noticeably loads the system.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Volumetric light: beams from lamps and flashlights are visible in air, dust and fog. Very atmospheric but heavy on the GPU.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]
Screen-space shadows on the player hands and weapon: the environment casts shadows onto the HUD.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Shadow cast by the player character body.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Dynamic sun shadows. The basis of daytime lighting. Without them the world looks flat, but it is one of the heaviest options.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]
Grass casts sun shadows. Heavy on the GPU in open areas.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Grass also casts shadows from local lights: flashlights, lamps, campfires.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]
Cloud shadows moving across the ground.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Sun shadow quality: cascade count and resolution, edge softness. Higher values give sharper and longer shadows, but the cost grows fast.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], VRAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Sun shafts shining through foliage and windows. Quality sets the number of ray-marching steps.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Shadow map resolution. Larger maps give sharper shadows with fewer jagged edges, but use more video memory.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Ambient occlusion: shadows in corners, crevices and under objects give the scene depth.
%c[255,240,240,240]SSAO%c[default] - fast classic variant, %c[255,230,190,60]medium cost%c[default].
%c[255,240,240,240]GTAO%c[default] - more accurate and softer, but %c[255,235,80,60]very heavy%c[default] on the GPU. Enable it only with plenty of FPS headroom.
%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.
%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]
Soft water edges: a smooth transition at shores instead of a hard line.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Soft particles: smoke, dust and fire do not get a hard cut where they intersect geometry.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Surfaces get wet in the rain and dry out afterwards.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

Screen-space reflections on water: puddles and ponds reflect the surroundings. Only what is visible on screen can be reflected.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Volumetric smoke and fog computed as a physical simulation. Beautiful, but one of the heaviest options.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default], VRAM %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Volumetric puddles on levels with reflections and ripples.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]

Puddles form during rain and evaporate afterwards.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default], VRAM %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Bullet, blood and dirt marks on characters and moving objects.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] CPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default], GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Darkening at the screen edges.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Chromatic aberration: colored fringes at the screen edges imitating a lens.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Saturation color grading for a more vivid image.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Gas mask or helmet glass effect: cracks, dirt and fogging on screen.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Rain drops on screen when the player looks up in the rain.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]

How rain drops on the glass are drawn.
%c[255,240,240,240]Texture%c[default] - a prebuilt animated texture, %c[255,110,200,90]almost free%c[default].
%c[255,240,240,240]Procedural%c[default] - drops are computed by a shader in real time, look more lively and realistic, but are %c[255,235,80,60]expensive%c[default] on the GPU.
%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,235,80,60]high%c[default]
Motion blur strength. Only the intensity changes: performance depends on the effect quality.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] %c[255,110,200,90]no performance impact%c[default]

Motion blur quality: samples per pixel. Higher gives smoother blur without banding.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Requires game restart.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,230,190,60]medium%c[default]
Overall volume of sound effects: footsteps, ambience, voices, mutants.
Volume of gunshots and explosions separately from other effects. Handy when gunfire is deafening and quiet ambient sounds are hard to hear.
Music volume: background themes, combat music, guitar and radio at campfires.
Sound output device: speakers, headphones, HDMI monitor and so on.
Combat music: during a fight the ambient theme switches to tense music and returns once the danger is gone.
EFX environment effects: reverb and echo depend on the place - caves, rooms and open areas sound different.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] CPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Mouse sensitivity when controlling the in-game camera.
Mouse cursor speed in menus, inventory and PDA, separate from in-game sensitivity.
Inverts the vertical mouse axis: moving the mouse forward tilts the camera down, like in flight simulators.
Which button icons to show in prompts: Xbox, PlayStation 4 or PlayStation 5. None - detect automatically from the connected gamepad.
Right stick sensitivity when controlling the camera.
Inverts the vertical axis of the camera stick.
Gamepad vibration on shooting, hits and explosions.
Gyro aiming: the camera turns when you tilt the gamepad. Works on gamepads with a gyroscope (DualShock 4, DualSense and similar). Handy for precise aiming.
Inverts the horizontal gyro axis.
Inverts the vertical gyro axis.
Gyro sensitivity: how far the camera turns when you tilt the gamepad.
Gyro dead zone: small movements and hand tremor are ignored. Increase it if the crosshair drifts while the gamepad is at rest.
Difficulty level. Affects damage taken by the player and dealt by enemies, as well as enemy accuracy. Can be changed at any time.
In-game text language: interface, dialogs, item and task descriptions.
How many quick saves to keep. A new quick save replaces the oldest one, so you can always roll back a few steps.

Three-dimensional scopes: instead of a flat full-screen scope texture you aim through the actual scope on the weapon, and the image is magnified. The surroundings stay visible around the scope. Works only on weapons that support 3D scopes.\n%c[255,150,150,150]Performance cost:%c[default] GPU %c[255,110,200,90]low%c[default]
Strength of camera and weapon bobbing while walking and running. Lower it if bobbing causes motion sickness.
When hit by a bullet or a blow, time briefly slows down and the aim gets knocked off.
Toggle aiming: one press enters aim mode, another press exits it. When off, you have to hold the button.
Automatic saves at key story moments.
Show the player weapon and hands on screen.
Toggle crouch: one press crouches, another press stands up. When off, you have to hold the button.
Show the crosshair in the center of the screen.
Dynamic crosshair: it spreads while moving and shooting, showing the current weapon spread.
Show the distance to the target in meters next to the crosshair.
Target info: the crosshair changes color depending on whether you look at a friend, a neutral or an enemy, and shows the character name.
Show the game HUD: health, ammo, minimap, indicators. Turn off for screenshots or full immersion.
Show the frames-per-second counter in the corner of the screen.
Show the minimap in the corner of the screen.
The quick slots panel hides automatically and appears when a slot is used or by a dedicated show quick slots key (bound in the controls).
Video memory
GB

Estimated video memory usage with the selected settings and the amount the system gives to the game. Updates as soon as you change options, before applying them.
%c[255,110,200,90]Green%c[default] - enough headroom.
%c[255,230,190,60]Yellow%c[default] - memory is almost full.
%c[255,235,80,60]Red%c[default] - not enough video memory, expect stutter and texture streaming.
%c[255,150,150,150]Texture and geometry usage is refined after a level is loaded: open the settings during gameplay for a more accurate estimate.
